content: <text>The system based on ESP32 and shows VPD, water level, and light trends. Remote, scheduled control for 2 water pumps with 80L tank is also provided. Roughly 30000lx @ 30cm with 6000-6500K LED running for 13-15 hours .</text>

<item>Day-neutral, everbearing strawberry cultivars: The supply nutrient water EC and pH are managed based on the root environment, with EC decreased upon growth to counter unequal nutrient usage and distribution.</item>

<item>Depending on growth and root status, leaf sprays of potassium phosphate and potassium nitrate (1-2mM each) are applied. which currently show perpetual exhaustion but runner development expected in summer.</item>
<caption>Strawberries: (Left) Root Propagation in Tap Water. (Right) Exhaustion from Untamed Fruitng and High Temperature.</caption>
<text>Cloning:  Shoots from the previous heirloom crop and seedlings from F1 seed are cloned. Sponges are used as a physical fix rather than a substrate .</text>
<item>Rooting is observed within 7 days. Starting from Day 14, the nutrient solution is managed at an EC of ~1.5 and a pH range of 5.2–5.7.</item>
<item>To suppress stretching and prepare for transplanting, the EC is boosted to ~3.0 just before the 1st flower truss blooms.</item>

<text>The container hold the starter solution, setted to an EC of 2.0–2.2 and a pH of 5.5–5.7. Following transplanting into this setup, over 90% of 1st flower truss fruited in all cloned seedlings.</text>

<item>4th tomatoes batch: Raised four varieties of heirloom seedlings using the same settings as previous batch. Seedlings from a shallow PS tray and small Grodan-sized sponges are cut into 5–7 pieces for substrate-less cloning.</item>

<item>This batch experiencing temperatures > 30°C and a VPD > 1.8 kPa, causing transpiration-without-growth issues. The water level in left first container has been intentionally raised and showing bad root development. Water is being added with an EC of 0.4–0.8 and a pH of 4.2–5.0.</item>
